17001: If your full motion video stutters, appears sluggish or is out of sync with the audio, try using these performance tips to help.
Full motion video requires the most processing power out of all the emulation functions that bleem! performs.
The sound that accompanies full motion video also requires lots of processing power.  Check your Sound Settings to be sure that they're set for maximum performance.
Using 8-Bit Samples and choosing Mono can improve performance greatly.
Turning off the audio completely will significantly improve the performance, but at the loss of the sounds and music for the video.  All other sound effects and CD music are not affected.

Enable "Black && White Only" to view your videos without color.  Greyscale images are much faster and can improve emulation speed.  This option only changes the portions of your game using motion video.  All other graphics are unaffected.
14001: Enable &Gouraud Textured Polygons (slower, but much better looking)
&Limit Maximum Speed (this will have no effect on slower machines)
Disable &FrameSkip (slower, but ensures all frames are displayed)
Enable &Alternate Display Updates (may be required for some games)
Enable Monitor &VSync (screen updates match with monitor refresh)

Many games use "Gouraud Textured Polygons" to achieve a smooth look, or sometimes for lighting and special effects.  Disabling this option usually makes games run faster, but can result in a "blocky" or "faceted" look.

Some higher-end machines, especially those that have 3D Hardware Accelerators, will run games far too quickly to actually play!  By enabling the "Limit Maximum Speed" option, bleem will slow down the game to a more playable speed.
Enabling any of the advanced options may cause bleem! to operate incorrectly.  To restore normal operation, simply uncheck all options.
20001: It's easy to automatically configure each of your controllers in just three steps:
1.  Select the Controller Type you want bleem! to emulate.
2.  Select the Input Device you want to use.
To change your controller emulation, just select a different Controller Type!
Upgrading to the latest drivers available from your Input Device and Sound Card manufacturers can improve the performance, compatibility and features available in bleem!
If you don't see your controller listed, that doesn't mean that it won't work with bleem!  Just select either Controller Tab above and configure it manually.
11001: Only use full screen when I've switched to it by pressing ALT-ENTER
Choose the best display mode automatically
If a perfect match exists, use it.  Otherwise, use this display mode
For the best performance, check "Always display in full screen."
Higher resolutions, or more colors, usually requires more processing power (and may run slower) than lower resolutions or fewer colors.
When bleem! chooses the display mode automatically, it picks the closest match to the original game settings, regardless of performance.
Choosing a display mode yourself forces bleem! to adjust the graphics to match the mode you selected.
Selecting a mode with lower resolution, or fewer colors, can greatly improve overall emulation speed, but may appear "blocky" or "pixellated."
Upgrading to the latest drivers available from your Video Card manufacturer can improve the performance, compatibility and features available in bleem!
18001: CD Recording Drives and CD ReWritable Drives are usually slower than regular CD-ROM Drives -- Choose your regular CD-ROM for better speed.
12001: &Don't resize the window automatically (usually slower when enabled)

Selecting "Don't resize the window automatically", forces bleem! to adjust the display to your window size.  This is usually slower due to the extra work involved in resizing the graphics, unless you make your window small.
&Remember the size and position of the window when restarting
Most machines perform fastest when using Full Screen mode instead of Windowed mode, but many will be able to run games in a window as well.
15001: Enable &Dynamic sound effects and music (may require fast machine)
Enable full motion &Audio effects and music
Selecting a lower frequency and using 8-bit Samples greatly improves the overall speed of emulation, and usually has little or no perceived difference in audio quality.
Stereo output requires twice as much work as Mono.
A high quality sound card and speakers is required to hear significant improvement in audio quality with higher frequencies and 16-Bit Samples.
Upgrading to the latest drivers available from your Sound Card manufacturer can improve the performance, compatibility and features available in bleem!

Some games use Dynamic sound effects and music that require very precise timing to operate correctly.  On some machines, the sound may be choppy, broken or stuttering.  Disabling this option doesn't affect gameplay.
